diagnostic.summary: Synthesized from 6 specialist agents · 24 data sources
diagnostic.text:
South Modern Trade Push underperformed despite an [n]18% increase in trade spend[/n] because the additional investment was eroded across three converging dimensions.
First, [r]retailer participation fell to 72%[/r], eight points below plan — 12 of 38 South retailers discontinued display by Week 4, pulling visibility out of B and C-class outlets.
Second, [r]average discount depth crossed the elasticity threshold at 18.2%[/r], with 7 SKUs running at 22% or higher where additional price cuts no longer generated incremental lift.
Third, [r]cannibalization within the portfolio cost an estimated ₹14.2 Cr[/r] as Premium Hair Care displaced Core Hair Care sales — and a competitor's parallel "Spring Saver" campaign captured [r]9 points of shelf[/r] across Chennai, Coimbatore, and Madurai.
Net outcome: [r]incremental sales of ₹24.8 Cr against a ₹38 Cr plan[/r] — an 18.3% gap driven not by under-investment, but by saturated levers and lost shelf control.

optimization.summary: Synthesized from 6 specialist agents · 22 data sources
optimization.text:
To maximize ROI on the upcoming Q3 Festive Push, the optimization engine recommends a revised plan that lifts modelled ROI from [g]1.53 to 2.18[/g]. No approved budget or policy threshold is defined in this project, so the plan is not judged against one.
[n]Channel mix should rebalance to MT 42 / GT 38 / eCom 20[/n] (from 50 / 35 / 15), recovering [g]₹3.2 Cr[/g] lost to sub-optimal allocation.
[n]Discount depth should be capped at 14%[/n] — the category sweet spot beyond which incremental lift plateaus.
Spend should concentrate on the [n]Top 20 SKUs[/n] that capture 78% of contribution, and a [n]0.7 percentage point lift in retailer incentives[/n] is modelled to drive [g]+12% participation[/g].
This is not a forecast, it carries no confidence figure, and no governance check is defined against which to pass it.

launch.summary: Synthesized from 6 specialist agents · 26 data sources
launch.text:
For the Q3 Festive eCommerce launch, the SKU prioritization analysis recommends concentrating [n]₹78 Cr behind 5 SKUs out of 32 candidates[/n] — SKU-A21, B14, C08, D33, and E12.
These 5 SKUs score [g]2.4× the portfolio average on brand equity[/g], deliver [g]92% historical conversion[/g] on Amazon and Flipkart Premium, carry [g]18% above-portfolio margin[/g], and have full inventory readiness with 6+ weeks of cover.
Category demand signal is [g]+34% YoY[/g], with search velocity up [g]42%[/g] on top-5 keywords.
One risk to monitor: [r]HUL Closeup and P&G Olay[/r] are launching parallel SKUs on B14 and D33 — competitive overlap should be actively tracked. This is not a forecast and carries no confidence figure.

strategic.summary: Synthesized from 6 specialist agents · 31 data sources
strategic.text:
The FY26 portfolio review recommends a [g]12% YoY increase in trade budget to ₹680 Cr[/g], deployed against a rebalanced portfolio mix that lifts projected category share from [g]14.2% to 15.8%[/g].
[n]Growth investment of ₹84 Cr[/n] funds the new Skincare range. [n]Regional allocation shifts +5 pp toward South[/n] where elasticity is highest, and [n]channel strategy moves +5 pp into eCom[/n] to follow consumer migration.
No governance or policy check is defined in this project, so the plan is not judged against one. Modelled ROI lift: [g]+0.18[/g].
Net effect: from [g]#2 to #1 category position[/g] by year-end, This is not a forecast and carries no confidence figure.
